Blame the cooks when the guests ask
An apology and an honest time keep the guests on your side. Silence makes ten minutes feel like thirty.
You spill red wine on a guest’s jacket. What do you never do?
Rub at the stain on the guest
Apologise to the guest at once
Hand the guest a clean napkin
You never touch a guest’s clothes. Apologise, offer a napkin, and the manager takes it from there.
Guests tell you they must leave in forty-five minutes. What do you do?
Tell the kitchen and suggest quick dishes
Take the order as usual and say nothing
Advise them to come back another day
Bring all the courses at the same time
Say honestly what can be done in the time, mark the order as urgent and have the bill ready early.
A guest asks something about a dish and you do not know. What do you say?
A guess can be wrong, and with allergens it can be dangerous. Checking takes a minute and earns trust.
A guest asks for something you cannot offer. What is the best reply?
Say what you can offer instead
Say that it is not on the menu
Say that nobody ever asks for it
Say the kitchen does not allow it
“We do not have that, but I can offer you…” turns a no into a choice. A bare no ends the conversation.
New guests walk in while you are busy at a table. What do you do?
Catch their eye and nod that you are coming
Finish first, then go and look for them
Call a greeting to them across the room
Walk away from your table at once
Guests forgive a short wait when they know they have been seen. Being ignored at the door is what they remember.
A shopska salad is tomato, cucumber, pepper, onion and, on top…
To a foreign guest: a fresh chopped salad under a “snow” of grated white brined cheese, a cousin of feta.
Tarator, the cold Bulgarian summer soup, is based on…
Yoghurt thinned with cold water, with cucumber, garlic, dill and walnuts. To a guest: a chilled yoghurt and cucumber soup.
What is the base of a Snezhanka (“Snow White”) salad?
Thick strained yoghurt with cucumber, garlic, dill and walnuts: in effect a tarator that you eat with a fork.
What is traditionally hidden in the banitsa on New Year’s Eve?
Each piece holds a “kasmet”: a wish on a slip of paper or a dogwood bud that stands for health, love or success.
Meat stewed slowly with onion, often in a clay pot
Minced meat grilled in the shape of a sausage
Cabbage leaves rolled around rice and meat
Tripe soup with milk, garlic and vinegar
Pork or chicken with onion and peppers, cooked long and served in its clay pot. To a guest: a rich Bulgarian stew.
Cabbage or vine leaves rolled around a filling
Peppers stuffed with rice and minced meat
Small dumplings boiled in a clear broth
Thin pancakes rolled around white cheese
The filling is rice, with or without minced meat. Vine-leaf sarmi are the Bulgarian cousin of the Greek dolmades.
What is the main ingredient of kyopolou?
Aubergine roasted over fire and chopped with roasted peppers, garlic and parsley. To a guest: a smoky aubergine relish.
Lyutenitsa is a spread made mainly from…
The peppers are roasted, peeled and cooked down with tomato in early autumn. Despite its name, it is usually mild.
Mish-mash is peppers, tomatoes and sirene cooked in a pan with…
A summer dish: the eggs are stirred in at the end, like a soft scramble, and it is finished with parsley.
What is brought to the table with shkembe chorba?
Garlic in vinegar and chilli flakes
Tripe soup is cooked mild, with milk and paprika. Each guest sharpens it to taste with garlic vinegar and dried chilli.
Which spice gives a kebapche its typical taste?
A kebapche is minced meat with salt, black pepper and cumin, grilled as a long roll. A kyufte is round and has onion.
Which herb gives bob chorba, the Bulgarian bean soup, its typical aroma?
It is spearmint, “dzhodzhen”, added near the end. Bean soup without meat is also a classic of the Christmas Eve table.
Patatnik is a speciality of which mountains?
Grated potatoes with onion and mint, cooked slowly in a pan until golden on both sides. “Patato” is the Rhodope word for potato.
Kapama is the winter speciality of which town?
Kapama belongs to Bansko and the Razlog valley. The clay pot is sealed with dough and left in the oven for hours.
In a kapama, several kinds of meat are layered and slow-baked with…
Pork, chicken, blood sausage and other meats go in with sauerkraut and red wine. It is a dish of the Christmas season.
The dish gyuvech takes its name from…
The clay pot it is baked in
The town where it was first made
The spice mix that seasons it
The cut of meat that goes into it
“Güveç” is the Turkish word for an earthenware pot. The small one for a single portion is a gyuveche.
What do all the dishes on a Bulgarian Christmas Eve table have in common?
It is the last evening of the Advent fast: beans, stuffed peppers, vine-leaf sarmi, pumpkin, dried fruit, walnuts and a ritual bread.
What is baked into the ritual bread of Christmas Eve?
The eldest at the table breaks the bread, and whoever finds the coin is said to have luck and plenty all year.
In Bulgaria, which colour is the first Easter egg dyed?
The first red egg is kept for health until the next Easter. The eggs are served with kozunak, a sweet braided bread.
Which dish is traditional on St George’s Day, 6 May?
St George is the patron of shepherds, so a whole lamb is roasted, often stuffed with rice and offal.
Which fish is traditional on St Nicholas’ Day, 6 December?
St Nicholas protects sailors and fishermen. The carp is usually stuffed with walnuts and onion; baked in dough it is a “ribnik”.
On which two days of the Easter Lent does Orthodox tradition allow fish?
The first and the last day of Lent
Useful with fasting guests: on the other days of Lent a strict faster avoids fish as well as meat, eggs and dairy.
On Sirni Zagovezni, what is swung on a thread for the “hamkane” game?
A boiled egg or a piece of halva
A red apple or a dried plum
A walnut or a dried pepper
A piece of bread dipped in honey
Everyone tries to catch it with the mouth, no hands. It is the last day of eggs and dairy before the Easter Lent.
Poached, on yoghurt, with paprika butter
Scrambled in a pan with peppers and tomato
Baked in a clay pot with sausage and sirene
The yoghurt is mixed with garlic and crumbled sirene, and hot butter with paprika goes on top. Turkish guests know a close relative: çılbır.
Kachamak is the Bulgarian relative of which Italian dish?
Both are cornmeal cooked into a thick porridge. Kachamak is served with sirene, butter or pork cracklings.
Cheverme, a tradition of the Rhodopes, is…
A whole lamb turned slowly on a spit
Lamb offal baked with rice and mint
A lamb soup with spring onion
Lamb stewed in a sealed clay pot
The lamb roasts beside an open fire for hours and is basted all the time. The name comes from the Turkish for “turning”.
The layers of a Garash cake are made from ground…
A Bulgarian classic: thin layers of walnut and egg white, chocolate cream between them and a dark chocolate glaze.
Unlike the Greek version, Bulgarian moussaka is built on…
Bulgarian moussaka is potato and minced meat under a baked topping of yoghurt and egg. The Greek one is layered with aubergine.
Honoured guests are traditionally welcomed in Bulgaria with bread and…
The guest breaks off a piece of the round loaf and dips it in the salt, often “sharena sol” mixed with herbs.
A set menu of several courses at a fixed price
A list of dishes that are priced one by one
A menu of cold dishes for a buffet table
A separate list of the desserts of the day
Literally “the host’s table”: everyone got the same meal at one price. Today it means a short set menu with little choice.
Many small courses in an order set by the chef
One large dish shared by the whole table
Free choice of three courses from the list
A buffet where the guests serve themselves
The guest tastes the range of the kitchen in small portions, so the pace and the story of each course matter more than size.
The French term “hors d’œuvre” literally means…
It stands outside the main “work” of the meal: small savoury bites before the courses, often passed with the aperitif.
A menu in the USA lists “entrées”. What are they?
In France an entrée is the starter, in North America it is the main. Check what an American guest means by it.
A digestif is a drink served…
From “to digest”: cognac, whisky, grappa or a herbal liqueur. Offer it with the coffee or after it.
The maître d’ (maître d’hôtel) is the person who…
Runs the dining room and its team
Leads the brigade in the kitchen
He or she takes the bookings, greets and seats the guests and directs the service: in our words, the floor manager.
In a restaurant, the “chef’s table” is…
A guest table in or facing the kitchen
The table where the cooks have their meal
The pass where the plates are checked
The largest table in the dining room
Guests watch the brigade at work and usually get a special menu, with the cooks presenting the dishes themselves.
What is the highest rating in the Michelin Guide?
Hotels can have five stars, Michelin restaurants at most three. Even one star puts a restaurant among the best in its country.
In Michelin’s own words, three stars mean…
Exceptional cuisine, worth a special journey
Good cooking at a moderate price
The guide began as a handbook for motorists, so each level is a travel tip: one star a stop, two a detour, three a journey.
Michelin’s Bib Gourmand is given to restaurants for…
The best wine list in the city
The work of a young head chef
It is not a star but a separate award for good value, named after Bibendum, the Michelin Man.
What do Michelin inspectors judge when they award a star?
The food on the plate and nothing else
Food, service and décor in equal parts
Above all the service and the wine list
Above all the comfort of the dining room
Stars go to the restaurant for its cooking: ingredients, harmony of flavours, technique, the chef’s personality and consistency.
In a classic French meal, when is the cheese served?
After the main course, before dessert
At the very start, with the aperitif
After the dessert, with the coffee
On the same plate as the main course
Savoury before sweet, and the cheese finishes the red wine. The British tradition is the other way round: cheese after pudding.
A beef stew in red wine
A baked dish of beans and duck
An onion soup under melted cheese
Several Mediterranean rock fish in a broth with saffron and fennel, served with toast and rouille, a garlic and saffron sauce.
Ratatouille is a Provençal stew of…
Summer vegetables stewed in olive oil with garlic and herbs, served hot or cold, on its own or beside meat and fish.
Cassoulet, from the south-west of France, is meats slow-baked with…
Duck confit, pork and sausage with white beans, baked in the “cassole”, the clay bowl that gave the dish its name.
The thin crisp top of a crème brûlée is…
“Brûlée” means burnt: sugar is melted on the cold custard with a blowtorch or under the grill, so it cracks under the spoon.
An upside-down tart of caramelised apples
A lemon tart under toasted meringue
A puff-pastry cake with almond cream
A baked custard tart with prunes
The apples cook in butter and sugar under the pastry, then the tart is turned over. Served warm, often with cream or ice cream.
Tournedos Rossini is a beef fillet topped with…
Named after the composer Rossini: fillet on a crouton, a slice of seared foie gras, truffle and a Madeira sauce.
A Chateaubriand is cut from which part of the beef?
The thick centre of the fillet
The rib, left on the bone
A thick piece of tenderloin roasted whole, usually for two, and carved in front of the guests.
The Burgundy classic is snails baked in their shells with garlic and parsley butter, eaten with tongs and a small fork.
Beef Wellington is a fillet of beef that is…
Baked in puff pastry with mushrooms
Roasted under a thick crust of salt
Braised in red wine with bacon
Smoked and served cold in slices
The fillet is seared, coated with duxelles (finely chopped mushrooms), wrapped in pastry and baked. It is carved in thick slices.
The name of the French pastry “mille-feuille” literally means…
The “leaves” are the many thin layers of puff pastry, stacked with pastry cream. Italians call it millefoglie.
Main dishes of meat and fish
The word means “before the meal”, not “against pasta”: cured meats, cheeses, marinated vegetables, bruschetta.
In an Italian meal, the “primo” is usually…
The order is antipasto, primo, secondo, dolce. Pasta is a course of its own, not a side dish to meat.
In Italy the meat or fish comes alone on the plate, so vegetables, potatoes or salad are ordered separately.
Grilled bread rubbed with garlic, with olive oil
Thin slices of raw beef with parmesan shavings
Fried balls of rice with a melting filling
Small soft dumplings of potato and flour
The topping of chopped tomato and basil is the best-known version. It is written with “sch” but said with a k: brusketta.
Where does a classic Roman carbonara get its creamy sauce?
Guanciale (cured pork cheek), eggs, pecorino and black pepper. There is no cream in the Roman recipe.
In a tiramisù, the sponge fingers are soaked in…
Layers of coffee-soaked biscuits and mascarpone cream under cocoa. The name means “pick me up”.
Ossobuco is a braised slice of…
The name means “bone with a hole”: the marrow in the middle is the prize. A Milanese classic, served with saffron risotto.
Saltimbocca alla romana is veal topped with prosciutto and…
A thin veal escalope, a slice of prosciutto and a sage leaf, fried in butter with white wine. The name means “jumps in the mouth”.
Cured hams hung up to dry
“Tapa” means “lid” in Spanish. Guests order several and share them, and a whole evening can be made of them.
Pintxos are the bar snacks of which part of Spain?
In San Sebastián and Bilbao the bar counters are covered with them. You take what you like and pay by the piece.
The cocktail stick that holds it together
The slice of bread underneath it
The bar counter it is served on
The pinch of salt sprinkled on top
“Pincho” means spike. Traditionally the bar counts the sticks left on your plate to make up the bill.
The wide, shallow pan it is cooked in
The fishing village where it was first made
The saffron that colours the rice yellow
The short-grain rice that goes into it
“Paella” is the Valencian word for the pan. The rice cooks in a thin layer, which is why the pan is so broad.
The toasted crust of rice on the bottom
The stock in which the rice is cooked
The mix of saffron and sweet paprika
The wedge of lemon served on the side
It forms when the last of the stock boils away, and many guests think it the best part. A paella is not stirred.
A cold soup of raw tomatoes and vegetables
A hot soup of garlic and stale bread
A thick stew of chickpeas and meat
A cold soup of yoghurt and cucumber
From Andalusia: tomato, pepper, cucumber, garlic, olive oil and vinegar, blended and served well chilled. Spain’s answer to tarator.
A thin flatbread of maize flour
A fried pastry filled with cheese
A rice dish cooked with seafood
Eggs and potatoes, often with onion, cooked slowly and cut into wedges. The Mexican tortilla is a flatbread, a different thing.
On a jamón ibérico, what does “de bellota” tell you?
The pigs were fattened on acorns
The ham was smoked over oak wood
The ham was cured for ten years
The pigs were raised in the mountains
“Bellota” is the acorn. In their last months the pigs roam oak pastures, which gives the fat its nutty taste and softness.
What is the top layer of a Greek moussaka?
Layers of fried aubergine and minced meat in tomato under a thick baked béchamel. The yoghurt topping is the Bulgarian way.
From the Balkans to the Middle East, “meze” means…
Small dishes shared at the start, with drinks
A thick soup served before the main course
A sweet pastry served with the coffee
A mix of spices for grilled meat
Dips, salads, cheeses, cured meats, small hot bites: the table fills up and everyone shares. The word came through Turkish from Persian.
İmam bayıldı is a Turkish classic. Which vegetable is stuffed in it?
Aubergine filled with onion, garlic and tomato, braised in olive oil and served cold. The name means “the imam fainted”.
Dolma is anything filled: peppers, courgettes, aubergines, tomatoes. “Sarma” means wrapped, and that is where our sarmi get their name.
How is the meat for shawarma and döner kebab cooked?
In a clay oven dug into the ground
In a covered pot, in its own fat
Thin slices are stacked on the spit and shaved off as the outside browns. “Döner” means turning, and so does the Greek “gyros”.
Hummus is a purée made mainly from…
